links.outcome: Sensitivity of classification performance to prompt strategy and few-shot example count
links.effect: Zero-shot micro-F1 0.716; few-shot k=2 0.652, k=3 0.693, k=4 0.654, k=5 0.696; CoT+SC 0.811. Performance varied non-linearly with number and selection of examples.
links.quote: The results reveal a non-linear relationship between the number of shots and model effectiveness.

links.outcome: Reference-standard construction (labels taken from original radiologist reports, no independent annotation)
links.effect: Reference labels were original classifications documented in the reports by radiologists, without independent blinded annotators or adjudication; reports contained discordance between measurements and stated conclusions.
links.quote: A reference set of original classifications, as documented in the reports, was retained for performance benchmarking.

links.effect: Accuracy and F1 reported with bootstrapped 95% CIs (3000 resamples); CoT+SC accuracy 0.81 [0.746-0.873]; per-class precision, recall, F1 reported.
links.quote: To quantify statistical uncertainty, 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for accuracy and F1-scores were estimated using non-parametric bootstrapping with 3000 resamples at the report level.

links.outcome: Single-site, retrospective, institution-templated data limiting representativeness
links.effect: Evaluation used reports from one institution with standardized RECIST-structured templates; authors state generalizability may be restricted and multicenter validation is needed.
links.quote: The use of single-center data may restrict generalizability due to stylistic homogeneity in report language and local reporting conventions.

links.outcome: RECIST classification accuracy versus expert labels
links.effect: Best CoT+SC accuracy 0.810 and micro-F1 0.81; zero-shot accuracy 0.72.
links.quote: CoT + SC achieved the best micro-F1 (0.81) and accuracy (0.810), exceeding the next-best approach (zero-shot, accuracy = 0.72) by an absolute + 9% points.

links.effect: k=2 few-shot micro-F1 0.652 versus zero-shot 0.716; CoT+SC reached 0.811.
links.quote: Adding just two examples per class (k = 2) led to a decrease in performance (micro-F1 = 0.652), indicating that limited contextual examples may introduce overfitting or noise, especially in a setting with imbalanced class distributions and variable linguistic structure in clinical texts.
